body.statement: Theorem 2 (SparseSIM-ID completeness). For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), under Theorem 1, \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) terminates after at most \(2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) exact rational-table checks and returns exactly one of two mutually exclusive certificates: either one observable arithmetic circuit \(\tau=(T_{D_0,y})_y\) with identities proving \(T_{D,y}=T_{D_0,y}\) on \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) for every \(D,y\), or \((D_0,D,p^{\dagger})\) with \(p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) and \((T_{D,y}(p^{\dagger}))_y\ne(T_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger}))_y\). The first branch occurs if and only if the intervention law is common to every represented DAG. On tied SA-MPDAG families this is a strict decision-theoretic tightening of Theorem 3.2 of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo: every query passing their sufficient graphical test is on the equality branch, while every query failing that test is still decided by an equality certificate or a rational positive separator. When \(\mathfrak G\) is a singleton and \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) equals its full positive Markov model, the decision agrees with Perkovic's single-MPDAG criterion and generalized truncated factorization.
body.justification: The theorem replaces arbitrary selection among tied sparsest graphs by an effect-complete common-functional-or-counterexample contract.
body.gap: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo prove only a sufficient simultaneous criterion; Perkovic is complete for one MPDAG rather than a tied family across MECs.
body.consumer: Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP all-ties output can report a common effect circuit or an exact ambiguity table instead of choosing one tied graph.
